name: Oracle

driver.license: Oracle Free Use Terms and Conditions

inputs.name: ca
inputs.label: CA certificate file (PEM) - only for a private CA such as AWS RDS or Azure; Enter to skip

access: CREATE SESSION and READ on each table of the schema (Oracle 23ai: READ ANY TABLE ON SCHEMA)

schema_check.statement: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM all_users WHERE username = {v}) THEN 'ok' WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM all_users WHERE username = UPPER({v})) THEN 'case:' || UPPER({v}) ELSE 'missing' END FROM dual
schema_check.case: Oracle stores a name in upper case unless it was created quoted

tips: Names arrive as Oracle stores them, normally upper case (EMPLOYEES): no quotes needed.
Oracle DATE carries a time of day, so it arrives as TIMESTAMP(0).
notes: The Java-only (thin) driver: no Oracle Client install. IMPORT FROM ORA stays off.
verify uses TCPS and checks the server certificate's name; the listener's TCPS port is often 2484, so set the port to match.

A CA (--set ca=<PEM file or bundle>) travels inside the URL as a trust-only PEM wallet (wallet_location=data:;base64,...), which ojdbc 23 reads with no file - so the loader's empty CA store on Exasol Personal does not matter. The short parameter name is required: oracle.net.wallet_location in an Easy Connect URL is ORA-12261. ojdbc 23 checks the host name with or without ssl_server_dn_match (measured: by IP, ORA-17965). Verified against RDS Oracle 19c SE2 over TCPS 2484.
